headline: Fixing timezone bugs in reporting queries with a simple helper
summary: Timezone bugs can cause reports to show incorrect data. A simple helper function can fix this issue.
details: A common issue in reporting queries is handling timezones correctly. When a report runs, it needs to know what day it is for each store, but stores can be in different timezones.

The problem arises when the reporting query uses UTC midnight for everyone, which can lead to incorrect data for stores east of GMT. The fix is to convert the store's local day-bounds into a UTC range before filtering.

However, there's a landmine in the conversion: if the datetime is already offset-aware, the localize() function will refuse to touch it, causing a ValueError. This issue can be solved by guarding the input before it hits datetime.combine().

The solution involves adding a per-store timezone field and a helper function that safely turns a local calendar date into a UTC range for filtering. This approach ensures that the reporting query is timezone-correct by construction.

The helper function normalizes its input before doing anything else, and Postgres handles the UTC comparison natively. This solution works for any date, not just 'yesterday,' and can be used for daily EOD reports, weekly summaries, and arbitrary date-picker queries.

headline_marked: Australia offers [[free daytime electricity]] from July 1, 2026
headline: Australia offers free daytime electricity from July 1, 2026
summary: Households in NSW, South Australia, and South-East Queensland to get at least 3 hours of free electricity daily
details: From 1 July 2026, energy retailers in NSW, South Australia, and South-East Queensland must give households at least three hours of free electricity every day. No solar panels required. No need to own your home. You just need a smart meter and to opt in through your retailer to have access to free daytime electricity.

The scheme is called the Solar Sharer Offer. It works by passing on the benefit of cheap midday solar power, which has always existed on the wholesale market but never made it to your bill, directly to households.
The free window will sit around midday, with the exact hours tailored to local conditions. As a rough guide, expect something like 11am to 2pm or noon to 3pm.
